teaching_units.title: Effects of Interest Rate and Exchange Rate Changes

evidence.exact_quote: Rising US interest rates led to an appreciation of the dollar.
When the domestic interest rate is increased relative to the rest of the world, the exchange rate must appreciate.
An expansionary domestic monetary policy leads to a contraction in output and an appreciation of the currency.
If the domestic interest rate changes while the rest of the world does not, the differential must be compensated.
Compensation for a higher interest rate differential comes through an expected capital loss on the currency.
The price of foreign currency in terms of domestic currency; it moves up (appreciates) when the domestic interest rate rises relative to the foreign interest rate.
The return on a bond or loan; when the domestic interest rate is higher than the foreign rate, the domestic currency tends to appreciate.
